answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by bonding every identity with a slashable stake that unlocks only after long honest service. A newcomer enters like a ship into a harbor: it posts collateral, and its reputation accrues slowly with each verified job. Since payouts scale with stake and history, a sybil farm must fund a separate bond per fake identity and keep each one active; when a cluster is caught, every bond burns. That turns a cheap swarm into an expensive, fragile nebula of accounts, and the steady pulse of slashing makes copied identities cost more than they can ever earn.
